findings.explanation: Vela's connect success callback acknowledges submission of the command. The watch starts MTU negotiation and service discovery there, before the link may be established. A discovery failure tears down the attempt, and the actual STATE_CONNECTED event does nothing. A mock following the documented callback order reproduced this retry loop. Start setup once on STATE_CONNECTED and use the command callback only to handle submission. [Vela Bluetooth API](https://iot.mi.com/vela/quickapp/en/features/system/bluetooth.html#GattClientDevice-connect-OBJECT)

The watch takes the first scan result and trusts its navigation payloads. A nearby peripheral with the same public service UUID can be mistaken for the owner's phone and supply false turn guidance. The name-only filter also admits an unrelated device, and the pinned-address branch drops the UUID filter. Require the full service UUID in every scan branch and authenticate the selected phone before accepting guidance. Address pinning alone only reduces accidental selection.

The NAV read permission and CCCD write handler expose street names, maneuver, remaining distance and ETA to any nearby central that connects. Even a central that never subscribes can read the current snapshot. Restrict both reads and CCCD writes to the owner's authenticated, encrypted watch connection. An open route feed is unsuitable for the planned public-road use even with a single owner.

The documented MTU callback supplies no negotiated value. The code reports the requested 185 as if confirmed, continues after negotiation fails, and can overwrite a low-MTU warning with a connected status. A peer that stays at MTU 23 can therefore leave the HUD waiting indefinitely with misleading diagnostics. Treat the callback as acknowledgment only and drive readiness and the low-MTU message from the phone's negotiated result or a verified payload exchange. [Vela Bluetooth API](https://iot.mi.com/vela/quickapp/en/features/system/bluetooth.html#GattClientDevice-setBLEMtuSize-OBJECT)

The fallback can exceed the negotiated payload budget. A representative core with a ten-digit session ID is 71 bytes, and the current serializer emits 94 bytes for that example with empty street and ETA. The builder keeps the optional keys and returns the result even below that size, so Android can attempt a notification that cannot carry the JSON. Omit optional keys as needed, return an explicit unfittable result when the core still exceeds the cap, and align the protocol's minimum with the actual encoding.

A successful subscription command resets backoff even when the CCCD write never takes effect. If the GATT link stays up with no NAV frames, there is no timeout to retry or resubscribe, including after a later notification stall. Bound setup and first-frame waits, recover after a sustained receive timeout, and reset backoff only after receiving a valid frame. [Vela Bluetooth API](https://iot.mi.com/vela/quickapp/en/features/system/bluetooth.html#GattClientDevice-setNotifyCharacteristicChanged-OBJECT)

Staleness compares the source age at send time and the watch's elapsed time independently. A frame received at age 9.9 seconds is still rendered 700 ms later and can show its arrow for almost three more seconds if heartbeats stop. A backward clock adjustment can also prolong or restore a stale arrow. Include time since receipt in source age and fail closed on backward time until a fresh frame arrives, or use a verified monotonic clock.

On disconnect the transport only reports status and retries. The page keeps showing the previous arrow through the disconnect and even into a quick reconnection until a new frame arrives or three seconds elapse. Invalidate the active channel's displayed guidance on link loss and retain the last accepted sequence separately so a duplicate cannot restore it.

Only a new vibration request cancels pending pulses. If guidance changes to idle, rerouting, arrival, an unknown maneuver or a new step outside the warning range, pulses scheduled for the previous turn still fire. The timer cancellation also cannot stop a pulse that has already started when the urgent pattern supersedes it. Cancel on invalidation and step changes, and use the documented cancellable vibration task API for active patterns. [Vela vibrator API](https://iot.mi.com/vela/quickapp/en/features/system/vibrator.html)

The notification builder captures the age and route state at poll time. The server stores that closure for future reads and subscriptions and stores serialized bytes under backpressure. If the phone main loop stalls and a subscription or completion callback arrives later, the watch can receive an expired instruction with a fresh-looking age. Keep the source timestamp with the queued snapshot and recompute age and expiry at actual read or send time.

Each demo tick marks the current Maps version as consumed while feeding the demo into the same throttle. When Demo is switched off, the latest Maps state is skipped until its version changes again. If no new notification arrives, the throttle can continue publishing the last simulated turn for up to 15 seconds. Force an offer of the current real snapshot on demo exit, including idle when no valid Maps source exists.

Listener connection never reconciles already-posted notifications. Granting access or rebinding during navigation leaves the HUD idle until Maps posts again. At line 42, removal of any ongoing Maps notification also clears the route even if a different key owns the current instruction. Seed from active notifications on connect using their actual age, track the selected source by key, and reconcile only when that source changes or disappears. [Android NotificationListenerService](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/service/notification/NotificationListenerService)

Rule order selects a maneuver from anywhere in the combined instruction. For example, “Turn right, then turn left” resolves to left because the left rule wins. An expanded notification can similarly override the primary instruction. Parse the first immediate maneuver from the primary field, use expanded text as a fallback, and suppress the arrow when the immediate instruction is ambiguous.

Arrival matching treats destination mentions and future imperatives as confirmation. For example, “In 150 m, arrive at your destination” becomes k=3 with d=0 and clears current guidance before arrival. Match explicit completed-arrival phrases and leave prospective arrival instructions in active navigation.

Unparseable distance tokens become 0 m. For example, “1,234.5 m” passes the distance regex but fails numeric conversion and can trigger the urgent pattern. The regex can also match the positive portion of a negative distance, and large values can overflow the final Int conversion. Return unknown on ambiguous or invalid tokens, reject negative and out-of-range values, and handle clearly grouped decimals before converting.

Street extraction can consume the maneuver itself. With title “150 m” and text “Vào vòng xuyến”, the split leaves an empty maneuver head and renders no roundabout arrow. Split off a street only after identifying an instruction prefix, or preserve the roundabout command for classification.

Only the current session ID is remembered. After the watch accepts session B, a delayed frame from session A is treated as another restart, can restore an obsolete arrow, and resets the vibration state. The live BLE and interconnect receivers share this filter. Reject retired sessions within the active receiver lifetime and preserve that history across reconnects.

Core validation accepts negative ages, nonpositive sequence numbers, distances below the unknown sentinel, negative exits and integers outside the safe JavaScript range. A negative age bypasses the freshness limit, and q=-1 for a different session can clear the current guidance before the frame is rejected. Validate domains before any session mutation. The UTF-8 decoder at line 43 also accepts malformed byte sequences, so validate decoding before parsing.

The in-flight gate is per peer, so a single broadcast can issue another notification before the server's onNotificationSent callback. Disabling and re-enabling CCCD at line 228 also clears the gate while an earlier send can still complete, allowing an old callback to release a newer send. Use one server-wide in-flight slot and retain only the latest pending payload per subscribed peer. [Android BluetoothGattServerCallback](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/bluetooth/BluetoothGattServerCallback#onNotificationSent(android.bluetooth.BluetoothDevice,int))

The CCCD handler accepts arbitrary two-byte values, including indication-only and reserved bits. It accepts nonzero offsets and prepared writes, then mutates subscription immediately without handling execute-write. A client can get a successful response for a subscription the server cannot honor. Accept only supported CCCD values at offset zero, reject prepared writes explicitly, and commit a subscription only after validation.

The optional system Bluetooth name can make the legacy scan response exceed 31 bytes, causing Android to reject the entire advertising request. A long personalized name is enough to make the watch see no service. Omit the scan-response name or retry without it on ADVERTISE_FAILED_DATA_TOO_LARGE. [Android BluetoothLeAdvertiser source](https://android.googlesource.com/platform/packages/modules/Bluetooth/+/refs/heads/main/framework/java/android/bluetooth/le/BluetoothLeAdvertiser.java)

Starting with Bluetooth off leaves an active foreground service that only polls the throttle. Turning Bluetooth back on never opens the GATT server. The same dead state can follow a Bluetooth toggle or a failed service registration. Stop cleanly on unrecoverable startup failure and rebuild the server when the adapter returns to ON during an active session.

Late GATT and advertising callbacks can run after stop, recreate peer entries, and overwrite the new service's shared BLE status and subscriber count. Response calls also read the mutable server reference outside its lock, and several Bluetooth operations can throw during adapter shutdown or permission changes. Reject callbacks from closed server instances, serialize server access with teardown, and route expected platform failures to service status.

Scheduling a retry releases the scanner and device before invalidating the attempt generation. A queued discovery or GATT callback can still act on the released attempt during backoff, including connecting after scanner failure or postponing the retry. Invalidate the generation before releasing resources and guard asynchronous callback bodies against a closed attempt and native exceptions.

Capture serializes extras, decodes and compresses two icons, and writes files synchronously in a main-thread notification callback before publishing the route. During the planned capture ride, slow I/O can delay both the new turn and the main-thread heartbeat. Publish navigation first and move capture to a bounded background queue. [Android NotificationListenerService](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/service/notification/NotificationListenerService)

The one-second heartbeat depends on a Handler using uptime. If the phone screen is off and the CPU suspends between Maps events, the foreground service can remain alive while the watch times out. Use a lifecycle-bound partial wake lock during active transmission if screen-off operation is required, or make the screen-on dependency explicit for this build. [Android Handler](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/os/Handler#postDelayed(java.lang.Runnable,long))

Starting the watch's local demo while the connected phone is idle works only until the next k=0 heartbeat, usually less than a second. The documented local layout and haptic check cannot complete with an idle phone connected. Keep demo and live acceptance state separate and exit the local demo when live navigation starts or the user taps to stop.

The phone Demo never reaches 50 m, so the planned BLE demo cannot exercise the urgent haptic pattern even though the phone README says it does. Make at least one demo maneuver cross both thresholds so the over-BLE setup can verify the urgent alert.

The advertised capture limit uses a process-local counter, counts sets of up to three files, and resets on restart. Retained route captures can therefore grow across sessions. Hashes and counters are committed before writes finish, so a failed export can also suppress the next attempt at the same capture. Enforce a persistent bound over existing capture sets and record dedupe only after successful writes. Add a way to clear the retained captures.

Every Start or Demo action requests POST_NOTIFICATIONS again after the user has denied it, even though it is optional for starting the connected-device foreground service. Gate those actions on Bluetooth permissions and keep notification permission in the separate permission action.

Keep-screen-on failures reported through the documented fail callback are ignored, and teardown never clears the request. If the runtime rejects the request, screen sleep can stop live BLE without any explanation. Handle asynchronous failure and release the keep-screen-on request when the page hides. [Vela brightness API](https://iot.mi.com/vela/quickapp/en/features/system/brightness.html)

Stopping detaches handlers and clears the poll timer, but already queued message and status callbacks have no active-instance check. A late message can reach the page after teardown or after a new receiver has started. Bind callbacks to the current connection generation and discard old callbacks after stop.

After the first BLE frame, the status line hides BLE status and retains the LIVE C label even on loss. It shows interconnect status while the actual BLE retry or error is suppressed. Clear channel liveness when invalidated and display the active transport's current status.

The contract still specifies the custom scan-response name MotoNavHUD, contrary to the approved system Bluetooth name decision and the phone README. Align the contract and watch README with discovery by UUID and the actual optional system name.

The root README still says both apps are unstarted and the project is in research. A reader following it misses the implemented build and sideload paths. Replace the status with the current prototype state and link the two app READMEs.

limits: Reviewed the supplied requirements, in-scope source and tests, and app READMEs. The directory has no Git metadata, so there was no diff or baseline for attributing older changes. Excluded research, spikes, generated output, and vendored files as requested.

Ran focused read-only Node probes for connection callback ordering, source age, session replay, and representative JSON byte counts. The reported unit-test, lint, APK and RPK results came from the controller and were not rerun.

No physical Watch S5, Android permission flow, BLE exchange, screen-off session, vibration, layout, or real Maps notification was exercised. Parser examples demonstrate behavior on synthetic input. Actual prevalence remains unverified.

The protocol says one vibration per step and also describes escalation from far to near. The implementation and tests choose one warning per threshold per step. The findings above concern cancellation and stale guidance under that interpretation.

Opt-in, Maps-only capture in Android's app-specific external directory is reasonable for the stated Android 13 and 17 lab devices. Exported raw captures still contain route details and should be redacted before sharing. [Android app-specific storage](https://developer.android.com/training/data-storage/app-specific)
